$$\text{CaCO}_3 + 2\text{HF (aq)} \longrightarrow \text{CaF}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$

The same kind of reaction will take place with Hydrochloric acid:

$$\text{CaCO}_3 + 2\text{HCl (aq)} \longrightarrow \text{CaCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$

So, the above reactions convince you that the elements of Group-17 exhibit the same properties and reactions. $\text{Mg}$ and $\text{Ca}$ of Group-2 also exhibit the same properties and reactions.

Magnesium Carbonate ($\text{MgCO}_3$) in its reaction with light Hydrochloric acid produces Magnesium Chloride, water and Carbon dioxide gas. Calcium Carbonate ($\text{CaCO}_3$), in the same reaction produces Calcium Chloride, water and Carbon dioxide gas.

$$\text{MgCO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \longrightarrow \text{MgCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$

$$\text{CaCO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \longrightarrow \text{CaCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$

**Name of Experiment:** Identifying Carbon dioxide gas in the reaction between Calcium Carbonate and light Hydrochloric acid.

**Principle:** Calcium Carbonate and light Hydrochloric acid produce Calcium Chloride, water and Carbon dioxide gas.

$$\text{CaCO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \longrightarrow \text{CaCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$

**Apparatus:** a. one conical flask b. a thistle funnel c. a u-shaped delivery tube made of glass d. some gas jars e. cork with bore.

**Chemicals:** Calcium Carbonate, dilute hydrochloric acid and water
